name: Explode
author: unknown

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 7. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. 131 keywords, and the widest overlap with anything already registered of the eleven that came off this archive: 18 of its names are claimed elsewhere, 7 by TURBO Plus, 4 each by EasyLife and AMCAF, 2 by CRAFT. Some of that is deliberate rather than accidental -- it declares `amcaf crack on` and `amcaf crack off` in its own table. The groups are a `rs *` structure allocator, packer front ends for BPK, DPK, IPK, PPK, XPK and LPK, a `plane *` bitplane block, fonts, and the usual system odds. The ExoticA wiki gives slot 7 (sharing with TOME) and names no author, pointing at the author's site https://testaware.wordpress.com/amiga/.
